name: Las Médulas
description: Las Médulas, in El Bierzo in north-west Spain, was the Roman Empire's largest open-pit gold mine. Roman engineers brought water down long aqueducts to collapse whole mountainsides, and the process left jagged rust-red cliffs and pinnacles. Nearly two thousand years on, the scarred hills stand among chestnut groves and farmland, and you can walk right through them.
